name: ZHĒNG FĒN
description: Zhēng Fēn ('Competing for Points') is a Chinese climbing/point-trick hybrid. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Shed cards through ascending combinations. Point cards: 5=5pts, 10/K=10pts. 100 total per hand. First out gets LAST player's tricks + remaining cards. Last out scores 0. Play to 500/1000.

content.text: Zhēng Fēn ('Competing for Points') is a Chinese climbing/point-trick hybrid. 54-card deck (52 + 2 jokers). Shed cards through ascending combinations. Point cards: 5=5pts, 10/K=10pts. 100 total per hand. First out gets LAST player's tricks + remaining cards. Last out scores 0. Play to 500/1000.

Zhēng Fēn (挣分, 'competing for points') is a traditional Chinese card game, a hybrid of climbing and point-trick (king-ten-five group). Documented in the West in 1985 by Axel Schmale in Pöppel-Revue after he learned it in China during a railway journey; it shares mechanics with Zheng Shangyou and Big Two and point values with Da Bai Fen (Hundred).
54 cards (52 + two distinguishable jokers, big and small).

Anticlockwise. First deal: a randomly chosen player shuffles, right-hand neighbour cuts. Players take one card at a time from the face-down pack, anticlockwise, until all cards are distributed; some may have one more card than others.
